GTA 6 Review
articles.chapeau: Is Grand Theft Auto 6 worth the hype? We
articles.txt:
What does eight years and an estimated $1 billion get you? Well, GTA 6 .
In this long-anticipated crime sandbox, Rockstar has assembled the most technologically accomplished open world ever made, expanding on its groundbreaking work with Red Dead Redemption 2 .
But crucially, with its dual protagonists Jason and Lucia, it’s grown up a bit.
This is the franchise at its most mature, shedding the cartoonish cultural caricatures of GTA 5 without losing the biting social commentary the series is known for.
The fictional state of Leonida is undoubtedly the star here; a dense and gigantic urban sandbox populated by an unfathomable array of art assets.
Whether it’s the easy-living coastal island of Key Lento or the mean streets of Crosstown, Rockstar’s artistry is utterly unprecedented.
Zoom in and you’ll see insects attracted to discarded food wrappers; a single convenience store has more unique art assets than entire districts in other open world games. This is remarkable stuff, delivered at such a scale it’s going to leave other publishers with their heads in their hands.
It feels alive, too; a casual visit to a gas station saw me berated by a cyclist for my wayward driving (I told him to chill out), while a brief pause on the side-walk ended up with my car getting hijacked by a masked criminal.
In over 150 hours of play, I’m still discovering random events that add depth and character to the open world. And even when the scripting is pushed to the background, the way every NPC feels designed, with distinctive personality and unique body types, makes this package an unfathomable feat.
But while Leonida is the standout, Jason and Lucia are the vehicles that guide you through it.
Just like GTA 5, each character has their own individual life, but the game is at its best when it brings them together.
I’ve never seen romance made into a mechanic quite like this, aside from perhaps the handholding in ICO , which is repurposed here. (Complete with DualSense haptic feedback when the characters touch.)
Jason is a bit of a beige blank slate, but Lucia brings genuine “girl power” to the story without pandering or feeling insincere.
In fact, in contrast to past GTAs, the many women in this instalment feel much more believable; the game frequently flips expectations on their head, without it ever coming across as forced.
A secret twist revealed in the opening moments adds gravity to the couple’s situation and becomes the driving force behind the story, which takes the pair from pillar to post, fulfilling the whims of a ragtag roster of ne’er-do-wells.
The campaign does fall into cliche territory at times, as the pair bounce from one bad idea to another in order to fulfil their ultimate ambition, and it’s something the characters seem to acknowledge. (“When are we going to get to call our own shots?” Jason wearily ponders at one point.)
But the mission design remains inventive throughout, regularly adding bespoke mechanics and interactions to keep things fresh.
In one early mission, Jason indulges his inner- PowerWash Simulator , as he rinses down a boat while other characters commentate key plot points. I won’t spoil the best moments, but needless to say there are missions here that will be remembered for a long time.
There’s also a slate of optional pastimes running concurrently to the main campaign which add genuine variety to the sandbox.
I was most enamoured by Jason’s home entertainment setup, which includes a distinctly PS4 coded console that can be powered up. I’ll leave you to discover his selection of fully playable games.
But beyond that, the ability to go hunting or even play a round of golf means you can lose yourself in this sandbox for hours at a time, and never really tire of the activities available to you.
Some of the action sequences remind me of all-time classics like Uncharted 3 – fist-pumping, set-piece heavy rollercoaster rides that push Rockstar’s engine to its limits, all within the confines of a meticulously designed open world.
Controller response is vastly superior to the studio’s previous games, with the cover shooting system feeling much more natural and the aiming mechanics buoyed by a pretty fun “bullet time” mechanic.
However, the game does fall into the trap of introducing heavily armoured bullet sponge enemies towards its conclusion, as it runs out of ways to make human-on-human encounters interesting.

articles.t: Grand Theft Auto VI review – gaming’s most depraved world is now also its greatest love story
articles.chapeau: With realism that defies belief, this vast game easily accommodates its trademark foulmouthed, OTT chaos – as well as new empathy for the fugitive couple at its centre
articles.txt:
The women can be as violent, visibly tough and deeply messed-up as the men … Jason and Lucia in Grand Theft Auto VI. Photograph: Rockstar Games View image in fullscreen The women can be as violent, visibly tough and deeply messed-up as the men … Jason and Lucia in Grand Theft Auto VI. Photograph: Rockstar Games Review Grand Theft Auto VI review – gaming’s most depraved world is now also its greatest love story With realism that defies belief, this vast game easily accommodates its trademark foulmouthed, OTT chaos – as well as new empathy for the fugitive couple at its centre
I n GTA VI, Rockstar has created the most extraordinarily, indulgently detailed virtual world that we have yet seen. Reviewing it feels a bit like trying to review, say, Paris: it contains so many potential experiences that it’s hard to know where to start. If you had been spying on me playing this game over the past few weeks you may well have caught me robbing banks, shooting up a weed farm or tearing along the highway at sunset blaring Bad Bunny on the in-game radio, but you might equally have caught me doing squats at the gym, shopping, assembling a coffee table or walking along the beach eating ice-cream. There is such a multiplicity of things on offer here that it is difficult to nail down what this game definitively is. Is it an interactive crime movie? A city simulator? A driving game? A sort of absurdly expansive version of The Sims in which the people you’re dressing up and looking after just happen to be professional criminals? It will be different for everyone – that is the beauty of it.
For me, though, this game is about Jason and Lucia, the fugitive couple through whom you experience all that Leonida has to offer. Jason is muscular, handsome, ex-military, steady and unflappable, sincere but spare with words. Lucia has been boosting cars since the age of 14, has a wicked sense of humour and takes zero bullshit. (Lucia is the scarier one; I found myself turning much more quickly to violence when playing as her.) At the start, Lucia is incarcerated and Jason is making a go of things in the sunbeaten Keys, working for a dodgy guy down on the marina and renting a run-down house on stilts with a jetty round the back and a pet snake. When Lucia gets out of prison, the two of them try to make some kind of life for themselves – but before long they get caught up with the wrong people and have to flee the cosy life they’ve just started building.
For a long time you really are two-bit criminals on the run, getting in with every dirtbag petty thief and drug-runner you come across in order to scrape some cash together and stay under the radar. You meet hillbilly pill-heads and biker gangs, friendly conspiracy theorists, a shady doctor, Lucia’s former prison friends and their lowlife boyfriends. By the time I actually got to Vice City – a glitzy den of sin, the centre of all Leonida’s pleasures and all its most extravagant criminality, where the gangbangers hustle on social media and even the narcos are obsessed with their Instagram clout – I had been playing for 30 hours. It took me 70 hours to finish the game and I could have taken longer.
Read more Leonida is so lifelike that at times it beggars belief, so vast that it feels overwhelming, and outside the story missions you can do whatever you please. There are nightclubs, gyms, flea markets, malls, restaurants, clothes shops, basketball courts, shooting ranges, aircraft hangars, projects and mansions, places to hunt and fish or go kayaking, gas stations and thousands of individuals engaged in conversation as you pass by. Interesting things are always happening in your peripheral vision. You might witness the cops chasing someone down to plant drugs on them, or overhear an interesting confrontation, or see a car speeding away and wonder where it’s going – though interesting things always seemed to happen when I was driving a stolen car at high speed towards a discerning buyer, or otherwise unable to stop and follow my nose. Thankfully, another opportunity would always present itself.

articles.t: ‘Grand Theft Auto VI’ is an astonishing American epic
6 things I loved about GTA 6, and 3 open-world learning curves gamers will hate initially
articles.chapeau: There's bound to be some divisive opinions
articles.txt:
GTA 6 does a lot right and is easily one of the best games of the year, but that's not to say it won't be controversial.
GTA VI is arguably the best work Rockstar Games has put out so far, and that should say a lot considering the sheer quality of its other open-world titles.
After 70 hours reviewing the game , my time in Leonida has been spent completing the main story, sampling side-content, and exploring every nook and cranny across the biggest map in GTA history.
It’s been a wild ride and I’ve loved every second, but my time with the game featured some steep learning curves I just know some gamers won't vibe with on a first playthrough. Here are six things I absolutely adored about GTA VI , and three things players might deem controversial.
With so many larger-than-life characters present across the Grand Theft Auto franchise, it’s hard to pick favourites, but Jason and Lucia are definitely up there for me after finishing the game.
Learning more about these star-crossed lovers, their history, and their motivations was an absolute treat, with Lucia in particular stealing the show.
Gone are the days of aggressive lock-on shooting and walking armouries. GTA VI borrows a lot from Red Dead Redemption 2 by restricting loadouts and forcing on-the-spot thinking.
It took a bit of getting used to, but once I did, combat encounters felt akin to John Wick-esque action scenes.
A mixture of long-distance and close-quarters gunplay and melee takedowns always had me thinking on my feet, as did scanning the environment for anything that could give me the edge.
While you do plenty of organised crime in the main story, there are loads of ways to make money while exploring the open world.
Jason and Lucia regularly meet new characters who’ll pay good money for their ill-gotten gains, and the variety of goods you can steal and fence keeps the money-making part of the game sufficiently varied. Performing these mini-heists also took careful planning and execution, from erasing security footage to securing an escape route.
Throughout the game, Jason and Lucia become more accustomed with the criminal underworld of Leonida - and as such, they pick up a few new tricks.
As you progress through the story, you’ll find handy tools and learn new skills that give you more options when it comes to break-ins and theft. I absolutely adored this. There are a lot of new gameplay mechanics in GTA VI and this slow-burn approach helps you learn the ropes at the same pace as Jason and Lucia.
The police aren't as aggressive here as they were in GTA V , but they're just as dangerous. They're also incredibly cunning. If my jewellery store robbery went wrong, the fuzz would waste no time setting up perimeters, and with hyper-vigilant helicopters and sniffer dog patrols, your escape is never guaranteed.
GTA VI also borrows the red zones from Red Dead Redemption 2 , meaning the police could recognise your appearance, clothes, and vehicle if you let them get a good look.
Vice City is as magical as it looks, and it far exceeds Los Santos, in my opinion. Your first introduction to the metropolis tells you everything you need to know about it, and one of the game's highest points is when you're finally free to explore it at your leisure.
As a real-life gym rat, I naturally gravitated to those locations first, but the beach, bars, and yes, even the strip clubs, all had their own flavour. Despite rolling credits, I'm still exploring and probably won't stop for quite some time.
Unfortunately, GTA VI repeats the same sin as GTA V ; most of the fun stuff is localised to one half of the map.
The southern section is solid. There’s plenty to do and plenty to see - and the bulk of the game’s missions take place there so you'll get plenty of time to explore. I enjoyed visiting the different towns and boroughs before returning to Vice City for another quick crime spree.
However, the northern part of the map is mostly forests, fields, and mountains. It’s like a miniature Red Dead Redemption 2 . While it’s just as gorgeous, you'll probably get flashbacks to GTA V's Blaine County, which was critiqued for its lack of content. Stick with it though. Just because it's void of skyscrapers and neon lights doesn't mean it's void of content.

articles.chapeau: GTA VI ships with 22 radio stations, the biggest and most varied dial Rockstar has ever built. Put those together with Rockstar’s October reveal and a picture emerges. articles.txt:
Gaming Gaming Tuning In to Leonida: Every Radio Station in GTA VI (GTA 6) OT Oliver Tryon — 19 November 2026 Share GTA VI ships with 22 radio stations, the biggest and most varied dial Rockstar has ever built.
Put those together with Rockstar’s October reveal and a picture emerges. Six stations come with celebrity hosts: Bad Bunny, Lana Del Rey, Morgan Wallen, Burna Boy, Robyn, Slayer’s Kerry King and Tom Araya, and Trick Daddy and Trina. Around them sit returning favourites like V-Rock, Flash FM and Emotion 98.3, a run of genre stations the series has never had (blues, jazz, classical), and a dedicated CircoLoco Records station for the club crowd.
Flash FM is Vice City’s pop institution reborn, hosted by Robyn and model Alex Consani. Rockstar previewed Charli xcx, MGMT, and Zara Larsson & PinkPantheress, but the in-game rotation reaches back too: Ciara and Justin Timberlake’s “Love Sex Magic”, Kylie Minogue’s “Spinning Around”, Drake’s “Hold On, We’re Going Home” and X-Press 2’s “Lazy” with David Byrne.
Emotion 98.3 returns from 2002’s Vice City with its soft-rock heart intact, playing The Cars’ “Drive”. Vice City FM , first glimpsed on a bus-stop ad, is the city’s ’80s new wave and pop station: Stevie Nicks’s “Wild Heart”, Echo & The Bunnymen’s “Lips Like Sugar” and Curiosity Killed The Cat’s “Name and Number”.
Stockyard FM , named after the Vice-Dale County town, is the indie-dance outlier: Justice & Tame Impala’s “One Night / All Night”, Neil Frances’s “You Move Me”, Fischerspooner’s “Emerge” and CMD/CTRL’s “No Stress”.
Dirty South Classics is pure Florida, hosted by Miami legends Trick Daddy and Trina. Alongside the previewed David Banner, JT Money and DJ Khaled tracks, it’s playing Juvenile & Soulja Slim’s “Slow Motion” and Petey Pablo’s “Freek-A-Leak”.
VCRR , a mystery when the wheel first appeared, turns out to be the modern rap station: Playboi Carti’s “Ahh Yeah”, BunnaB’s “Go Go Go”, Drake’s “Nokia”, Gunna’s “Count Up”, Pooh Shiesty’s “Got Dat” and Offset’s “I Just Came To Pop It”. Old-school Southern rap on one frequency, current trap on the next.
Honey FM , whose logo had been spotted on a taxi, is the ’90s R&B and soul slow-jam station: D’Angelo’s “Lady”, Sounds of Blackness’s “Optimistic”, Zhané’s “Hey Mr. DJ” and Montell Jordan’s “Get It On Tonite”.
Cocoteo FM is the headline Latin station, with Bad Bunny hosting as “El Martillo” next to RaiNao’s “La Gata”. It mixes reggaeton, dembow and bachata: Bad Bunny’s “EoO” and Romeo Santos from the official preview, plus Anuel AA & Haze’s “Amanece” and Young Miko’s “Ni Le Cabe” in game.
Radio La Ola is its golden-age counterpart, playing Cachao’s “Descarga Cubana”, El Gran Combo de Puerto Rico’s “No Hay Cama Pa’ Tanta Gente”, Celia Cruz and Johnny Pacheco’s “Besito de Coco”, Gloria Estefan’s “Mi Tierra” and Banda Blanca’s “Sopa de Caracol”.
Radio On-U takes its name from Adrian Sherwood’s On-U Sound dub label, and Sherwood’s own “Dub Inspector” is in rotation. The rest is roots and lovers rock: Louisa Mark’s “Caught You in a Lie”, Carroll Thompson’s “I’m So Sorry” and Freddie McGregor’s “Big Ship”.
V-Rock is back with its vulture logo, though it now leans classic rock over hair metal: Bon Jovi’s “Runaway”, The Rolling Stones’ “Emotional Rescue” and Huey Lewis & The News’s “I Want a New Drug”.
The heavier stuff moves to The Chamber 106.6 , hosted by Slayer’s Kerry King and Tom Araya. Beside their own “Raining Blood” and the previewed Black Sabbath and Pantera tracks, it plays Megadeth’s “Symphony of Destruction” and Metallica’s “Master of Puppets”, so Slayer are spinning their Big Four rivals.
Back Country Radio has the strangest host pairing in the game: Morgan Wallen as “MW” and Lana Del Rey as “Delta Dawne”, with Jeremy Dufrene filing weather reports from an airboat as “Mud Dog Mike”. It’s outlaw and classic country, from David Allan Coe’s “Need a Little Time Off for Bad Behavior” to Mel McDaniel’s swampy “Louisiana Saturday Night”.
This is where GTA VI breaks new ground: three stations for genres the series has never given their own frequency.
Gloriana Blues Radio runs from pre-war gospel blues to Chicago electric: Ella Fitzgerald’s “Trouble in Mind”, Memphis Minnie’s “Me and My Chauffeur” (credited in game with Little Walter), Jimmy Rogers’s “That’s All Right”, John Lee Hooker’s “Boogie Chillen'” and Sister Rosetta Tharpe’s “Didn’t It Rain”.

articles.txt:
The famous Vice City pop station returns with Robyn and Alex Consani hosting a new generation of pop, dance and alternative hits.
Rockstar describes Flash FM as a Vice City institution delivering pop music and “guaranteed grooves” across Leonida. The official pre-release station preview has already revealed music from Charli xcx, MGMT, Zara Larsson and PinkPantheress.
As of 18 November 2026, three tracks have been identified from Rockstar’s official Flash FM preview:
The full in-game playlist has not yet been officially published.
That should change quickly once GTA VI is fully available around the world on 19 November.
Robyn is one of Sweden’s most influential pop performers, known for songs including “Dancing on My Own”, “Call Your Girlfriend” and “With Every Heartbeat”.
The combination makes sense for a station designed around contemporary pop culture rather than a conventional fictional DJ.
But the three songs revealed before launch suggest Rockstar is using a fairly broad definition.
MGMT’s “Electric Feel” is psychedelic electronic pop from the late 2000s.
Zara Larsson and PinkPantheress connect current mainstream pop with UK dance influences.
That means Flash FM does not appear to be restricted to one period.
It looks more like a modern pop station built around songs that feel good driving through Vice City.
Flash FM originally appeared in Grand Theft Auto: Vice City, where its 1980s pop soundtrack became closely associated with driving around Rockstar’s fictional version of Miami.
Bringing the name back immediately creates nostalgia for longtime GTA players.
GTA VI’s version is built around contemporary and more recent pop.
“Good Ones” is one of the first tracks heard in Rockstar’s Flash FM preview.
Released during Charli xcx’s pop-focused era, the song combines synthesizers with an immediate dance rhythm.
It fits Flash FM particularly well because Charli occupies the space between mainstream pop and club music.
Her inclusion also reflects how much that sound has influenced pop during the 2020s.
A player who discovers Charli through GTA VI has a huge catalogue waiting behind this one track.
The oldest song currently confirmed for Flash FM is also one of its most recognisable.
MGMT released “Electric Feel” on their 2007 album Oracular Spectacular.
The song combines psychedelic pop, electronic production and a distinctive bassline.
The recording already feels nostalgic to listeners who grew up during the late 2000s, in the same way 1980s songs felt nostalgic inside the original Vice City.
The third pre-release selection brings the station directly into 2026.
Zara Larsson and PinkPantheress represent two different sides of contemporary pop.
PinkPantheress brings influences from UK garage, drum and bass and internet-era dance music.
Together they give Flash FM a more current sound than its original Vice City incarnation.
The three songs currently known come from a short station preview, not the complete broadcast.
Rockstar says GTA VI contains its biggest and widest-ranging selection of in-game radio and podcasts yet.
That makes it extremely unlikely that Flash FM will contain only three tracks.
The full list should become clearer as players spend more time driving around Leonida after launch.
Rockstar has revealed six stations ahead of launch, but its own description refers to a much broader radio and podcast selection.
Radar has a full guide to the announced stations and their hosts here: GTA 6 Radio Stations Revealed: Bad Bunny, Lana Del Rey, Burna Boy and More Confirmed .
Flash FM looks likely to become the easiest GTA VI station for listeners who want the game to double as a constantly changing pop playlist.
The confirmed pre-release songs are Charli xcx’s “Good Ones”, MGMT’s “Electric Feel” and Zara Larsson and PinkPantheress’ “Midnight Sun (Girls Trip)”.
The complete tracklist is expected to be considerably larger and should be updated here as new songs are verified after GTA VI launches.

articles.chapeau: From violence and strong language to online features and in-game purchases, here’s everything parents need to know about GTA VI
articles.txt:
0 Share Newsweek is a Trust Project member See more of our trusted coverage when you search. Prefer Newsweek on Google to see more of our trusted coverage when you search. The anticipation surrounding the release of Grand Theft Auto VI could hardly be greater.
Evidence of that arrived long before the game itself. GTA VI's debut trailer attracted more than 90 million views within 24 hours, setting a Guinness World record for the most-viewed video game reveal on YouTube in a single day.
While many gamers are counting down the days until they can explore Rockstar's latest open-world adventure, some parents may be keen to take a closer look at the game's age rating before deciding whether it's appropriate for their children.
Like every previous entry in the blockbuster Rockstar Games franchise, GTA VI features mature themes and content that have led ratings boards to classify it as suitable only for “mature” players.
From violence and strong language to online features and in-game purchases, here's everything parents need to know about GTA VI's age rating, content warnings and parental controls.
The Entertainment Software Rating Board (ESRB), the independent non-profit body that assigns age ratings and content warnings to video games in the United States, has awarded GTA VI an M (Mature 17+) rating, indicating the game is intended for players aged 17 and older.
The ESRB stopped short of assigning GTA VI an AO (Adults Only 18+) rating, the category reserved for games intended exclusively for adult audiences. The classification also differs slightly from that used in Europe and the U.K., where the game has received an 18 rating from Pan European Game Information (PEGI), the age-rating system used across more than 40 European countries. Newsweek has contacted the ESRB for comment.
According to the ESRB, GTA VI received its Mature 17+ rating because it contains "blood and gore, intense violence, mature humor, nudity, strong language, strong sexual content, [and] use of drugs and alcohol."
GTA VI is not considered suitable for children because it features graphic violence, sexual content, nudity, strong language, and depictions of drug and alcohol use. As a result, ratings boards on both sides of the Atlantic have classified the game as being intended for older players rather than children and younger teenagers.
Some experts believe it's important for parents to look beyond the rating system though.
Jamie Krenn is an Adjunct Associate Professor at Teachers College, Columbia University, and Guest Faculty at Sarah Lawrence College. She teaches courses at both institutions focusing on media processing specifically with children and told Newsweek that while the ESRB rating is a “useful starting point” it shouldn’t replace parent involvement and conversations about media.
“Children and adolescents differ in their cognitive and emotional development, and that matters when thinking about video games,” Krenn said. “Just because a teen is interested in a game, or their friends are playing it, doesn’t mean they are ready for its content. Parents should consider not just the presence of violence, sexual content, or drug use, but also how these behaviors are portrayed and understood by their children.”
Krenn said it’s important to understand that every child is different in what they understand and can handle. “The broader context matters,” she said. “Rather than assuming that exposure to mature content will necessarily lead to negative outcomes, parents should think about their child’s maturity, sensitivity to certain content, and ability to distinguish fictional scenarios from real-world behavior.”
The official ESRB rating states that GTA VI features “in-game purchases.” In-game purchases allow players to spend real money on digital items or content within the game they are playing. Rockstar Games has not yet disclosed exactly what those purchases will entail.
The franchise's previous online component, GTA Online , offered optional micro transactions through “Shark Cards.” These allowed players to purchase in-game currency with real money. However, Rockstar has yet to confirm whether GTA VI will use the same system or introduce a different monetization model.
While the ESRB rating is primarily driven by the game's violent and sexual content, some experts have also raised concerns about the potential impact of in-game spending on younger players.

articles.t: GTA 6: origines écossaises, provoc' et polémiques... Comment Rockstar a surfé sur la subversion depuis les 90's
articles.chapeau: Le sixième opus de la célèbre franchise du studio Rockstar Games sera enfin jouable jeudi à minuit. Aux origines de ce mastodonte vidéoludique, une entreprise écossaise qui assume, dès la fin des années 90, de proposer un jeu prônant l'immoralité et axé sur la violence.
articles.txt:
Le sixième opus de la célèbre franchise du studio Rockstar Games sera enfin jouable jeudi à minuit. Aux origines de ce mastodonte vidéoludique, une entreprise écossaise qui assume, dès la fin des années 90, de proposer un jeu prônant l'immoralité et axé sur la violence. Ce jeudi 19 novembre, à minuit, sortira enfin le jeu vidéo GTA 6 . Avant même sa sortie, le jeu est déjà un succès commercial. Il a enregistré 15 millions de précommandes dans le monde, un record historique. Et qui dit précommandes dit recettes : 1,5 milliard de dollars, c'est ce qu'a déjà généré GTA VI. De quoi permettre au jeu d'être pratiquement à l'équilibre financier avant même sa commercialisation. Bref, les conditions du triomphe sont réunies.
Chevallier remonte le temps : Aux origines de GTA, une provocation assumée - 18/11 3:05 Rockstar Games, un studio écossais Et pourtant, au départ, rien ne prédestinait ce jeu au succès. Pour remonter aux origines de GTA, ce n'est pas aux États-Unis qu'il faut aller, mais en Écosse. Tout a commencé là-bas, dans les années 1990, à Dundee. Un petit studio développe alors un jeu de voitures en 2D. Rien de bien extraordinaire. Le projet devait s'appeler "Race n' Chase", soit "course et poursuite" en français.
Mais le concept évolue. Finalement, le jeu devient révolutionnaire : le joueur peut tout faire, ou presque. Aller n'importe où, agresser qui il veut, tirer sur n'importe quel passant. Et surtout, voler n'importe quelle voiture, au risque d'être pourchassé par la police. Bref, le concept consiste à vivre la vie d'un véritable voyou. D'où le titre final : "Grand Theft Auto". Dans le code pénal californien, cette expression désigne un vol de voiture aggravé.
Le côté subversif était donc assumé dès le début. ll va même devenir un argument de vente. En 1997, quelques mois avant la sortie du jeu, l'éditeur embauche une agence de communication pour en assurer la promotion. Et celle-ci va avoir une idée de génie : mettre en avant les aspects immoraux de GTA, du vol à la violence, en passant par les agressions contre la police. Le tout pour faire le buzz et s'arranger pour que des responsables politiques en entendent parler.
Et ça fonctionne... C'est un membre de la Chambre des lords, l'une des deux chambres du Parlement britannique, qui se saisit du dossier. Un vieux lord de 75 ans, très conservateur, qui interpelle le Premier ministre de l'époque, Tony Blair. Il réclame que le gouvernement interdise purement et simplement ce jeu scandaleux.
La demande n'aboutit pas, mais le buzz est assuré. Lorsque GTA sort, le 28 novembre 1997, il s'en vend un million d'exemplaires en moins d'un an. Vous voyez donc que les scandales liés à GTA et les reproches concernant la violence du jeu n'ont rien de nouveau. C'est même l'une des clés de son succès.

Prefer Newsweek on Google to see more of our trusted coverage when you search. Scores of gamers around the world are risking their accounts to play Grand Theft Auto VI early by exploiting a loophole in the Xbox’s hardware known as the New Zealand trick.
On social media, gamers have reported accessing the game early after using the New Zealand trick, with plenty of players reporting the exploit works as intended on Xbox. Newsweek could not independently verify id this was indeed the case.
GTA 6 goes on sale at midnight today, with its release being staggered across local time zones around the world. That means the first country with access to the game is New Zealand as its time zone, GMT+13, is further forward than anywhere else in the world.
U.S. Xbox players using the so-called New Zealand trick could begin playing GTA 6 as early as 6 a.m. ET on Wednesday, 18 hours before its official U.S. release.
The New Zealand trick involves changing your console’s regional settings to NZ, taking advantage of the time zone to unlock games early. The trick has been used many times in the past by gamers on a variety of titles.
New Zealand has taken full advantage of the boost in popularity the game’s release has provided, with the country’s official tourist board advertising early access to the game.
"One perk of seeing the sun first? Getting GTA 6 first too," an Instagram post by the tourist board read. "We heard a few of you are trying the New Zealand trick to join us. We get it, and we'd love to have you."
While the New Zealand trick may appear safe, with many gamers saying they have used it to get their hands on the game early, the trick—which involves changing the regional settings on your console to appear in NZ—is technically in violation of Microsoft’s Terms of Service, and a number of gamers have reported having their accounts suspended for attempting to circumvent the rules.

© Rockstar Games Après deux reports, GTA 6 arrive ce jeudi 19 novembre sur PS5 et Xbox Series X. La question que tous les joueurs se posent reste donc : quand pourra-t-on enfin lancer sa partie et jouer au jeu vidéo ? Serieously vous explique tout et, une chose est sûre : les utilisateurs de PC risquent d’être déçus…
Il ne reste plus que quelques heures à attendre… Le 19 novembre prochain, les joueurs du monde entier pourront enfin se rendre dans la ville fictive de Vice City et découvrir les nouvelles aventures qui attendent Jason et Lucia dans le tant attendu GTA 6 .
Pour autant, qui dit sortie mondiale dit également heures de sortie différentes en fonction des régions du monde . Par exemple, si un jeu vidéo est disponible à minuit, heure de Los Angeles aux États-Unis, cela équivaut à une sortie à 9h du matin dans l’Hexagone. Mais alors, qu’en est-il de GTA 6 ? À partir de quelle heure les fans français pourront-ils lancer officiellement leur jeu vidéo ?
Pour GTA 6 , la règle est un peu différente. En effet, le jeu vidéo phénomène ne se base pas sur un fuseau horaire particulier , mais sur une date globale. Ainsi, i l se débloquera à minuit dans chaque fuseau horaire, dans la nuit du mercredi 18 au jeudi 19 novembre . En France métropolitaine, les joueurs pourront donc commencer à jouer dès minuit, heure de Paris.
Pour être prêt à cette heure-là, il est possible de précharger le jeu depuis le mardi 10 novembre. Attention toutefois à la place nécessaire : le fichier du jeu vidéo peut atteindre 212 Go et des mises à jour risquent d’être publiées au moment de l’ouverture des serveurs.
Ce téléchargement concerne également les acheteurs de la version en boîte, car celle-ci contient un code et non un disque. Une connexion internet sera donc nécessaire avant de pouvoir jouer, même avec un exemplaire physique.
Si vous faites partie de la communauté des joueurs PC, l’attente sera malheureusement encore plus longue. La sortie de ce jeudi concerne, en effet, uniquement la PS5 et la Xbox Series X . Pire, aucune date officielle n’a encore été annoncée pour la version PC . Contrairement aux joueurs sur console, vous ne pourrez donc pas profiter du déblocage prévu à minuit.
Selon les dernières rumeurs, une période circule néanmoins : une sortie sur PC serait visée pour le premier trimestre 2027 . Ce calendrier n’est pas une annonce officielle et ne fixe pas de jour précis. Pour l’heure, aucun motif n’a été communiqué dans l’annonce de cette sortie sur consoles pour expliquer le décalage avec le PC. Affaire à suivre donc.

GTA 6 sur PS5 : les réglages indispensables à appliquer avant jeudi pour jouer dans les meilleures conditions — Frandroid
articles.chapeau: GTA 6 sort ce jeudi 19 novembre sur PS5, avec jusqu'à 212 Go à installer et une cible de 30 images par seconde, PS5 Pro comprise.
articles.txt:
Après des années d’attente, GTA 6 arrive enfin sur console. Vous l’avez même sans doute déjà préchargé sur votre PS5 ou votre PS5 Pro.
Rockstar a confirmé le 10 novembre que le jeu vise 30 images par seconde sur toutes les consoles, PS5 Pro comprise, sans mode performance. Il se débloque ce jeudi 19 novembre à minuit, heure locale. Voici les réglages à faire sur la PS5 d’ici là.
Rockstar annonce que le jeu demande jusqu’à 212 Go selon la console . Deux mises à jour sont déjà arrivées avant la sortie sur PS5, d’environ 1 Go le 13 novembre puis 600 Mo le 16 novembre, d’après Forbes . Rockstar n’a pas annoncé d’autre patch pour jeudi. Prévoyez donc 250 Go libres pour garder de la marge. La version en boîte ne vous fera pas gagner de place, puisqu’elle ne contient qu’un code de téléchargement. Entrez ce code dès que vous recevez le jeu : le préchargement démarre tout de suite, sans attendre jeudi.
Sur une PS5 de 825 Go, il ne reste qu’environ 667 Go utilisables une fois le système installé : GTA 6 en prendra donc à lui seul un tiers. Faites le tri dans Paramètres > Stockage > Stockage console > Jeux et applications, et désinstallez ce que vous ne lancez plus. Les jeux PS4 peuvent aller sur un disque dur USB, depuis lequel ils se lancent normalement. Un jeu PS5 peut aussi y être rangé, mais il faudra le recopier sur le stockage interne pour y jouer.
Si la place manque vraiment, la PS5 accepte un SSD supplémentaire dans sa baie d’extension, cachée sous la coque. Il doit s’agir d’un SSD M.2 NVMe PCIe 4.0, le format de petites barrettes rapides avec lequel la console peut faire tourner des jeux PS5. Choisissez-en un compatible PS5 et équipé d’un dissipateur, la plaque de métal qui l’empêche de trop chauffer.
Côté console, tout se passe dans Paramètres > Écran et vidéo > Sortie vidéo. Laissez la résolution sur Automatique, ou choisissez 2160p si votre téléviseur est en 4K.
Pour le HDR, qui élargit l’écart entre les zones sombres et lumineuses de l’image, sélectionnez « Activé si pris en charge » plutôt que « Toujours activé », qui force le HDR même sur les contenus qui n’en ont pas. Lancez ensuite la calibration HDR et suivez ses trois écrans de réglage en vous aidant des repères de votre téléviseur.
Sur le téléviseur , activez le mode Jeu. Il coupe une partie des traitements d’image pour réduire la latence, c’est-à-dire le délai entre l’appui sur la manette et l’action à l’écran. Désactivez aussi les « améliorations » de mouvement comme l’interpolation, qui invente des images intermédiaires pour lisser l’affichage : à 30 images par seconde, elle ajoute du retard et des défauts visibles autour des objets en mouvement. Si votre téléviseur gère l’ ALLM , le mode faible latence automatique, il passe de lui-même en mode Jeu quand la PS5 s’allume.
Le VRR, qui cale le rafraîchissement de l’écran sur le rythme réel du jeu pour limiter les saccades, et la sortie 120 Hz peuvent rester sur Automatique. Ils ne gênent pas, mais Rockstar n’a confirmé ni l’un ni l’autre. On active donc par précaution.
La PS5 Pro reste elle aussi à 30 images par seconde, avec deux améliorations graphiques en plus. D’abord le PSSR, la technique de Sony qui s’appuie sur l’IA pour produire une image plus nette à partir d’une définition plus basse. Ensuite, des ombres calculées en ray tracing , c’est-à-dire en simulant le trajet de la lumière. La PS5 standard n’y a pas droit.
Les propriétaires de PS5 Pro n’ont aucun réglage supplémentaire à activer, puisque Rockstar n’indique pas d’option pour couper ou ajuster le PSSR et les ombres en ray tracing . Vérifiez seulement que la console est à jour (Paramètres > Système > Logiciel système) et que l’option qui active le PSSR amélioré est cochée dans Paramètres > Écran et vidéo > Sortie vidéo.

articles.t: GTA 6 a-t-il tiré un trait sur "le plus vieux métier du monde" de Vice City ?
articles.chapeau: Mais si, vous savez exactement de quoi on parle, ne faites pas semblant. C’est l’une des traditions les plus polémiques de la série, et beaucoup de joueurs se demandaient si elle survivrait à 2026. On a arpenté Vice City de nuit pour en avoir le cœur net.
articles.txt:
Mais si, vous savez exactement de quoi on parle, ne faites pas semblant. C’est l’une des traditions les plus polémiques de la série, et beaucoup de joueurs se demandaient si elle survivrait à 2026. On a arpenté Vice City de nuit pour en avoir le cœur net.
Chaque GTA traîne ses polémiques, et celle-ci revient à tous les épisodes depuis plus de vingt ans . Avec un GTA 6 scruté comme aucun jeu avant lui, on se demandait donc ce que Rockstar allait faire de ses fameuses dames de la nuit . Forcément on est allé vérifier, pour la science évidemment.
Pour comprendre pourquoi la question se pose, il faut rappeler d’où on vient. La série n’a jamais sorti un épisode sans prostituées depuis GTA III , en 2001, et GTA 5 ne fait pas exception . On les y croise la nuit dans les rues de Los Santos, avec des tarifs allant de 50 à 100 dollars, et ça n’a pas été sans conséquence. En 2014, les chaînes Target et Kmart ont retiré le jeu de leurs rayons en Australie, après une pétition lancée par d’anciennes prostituées qui avait dépassé les 40 000 signatures.
Pour ce qui est des filles de joie dans GTA 6 , on n’en a vu aucune dans les rues de Vice City ni ailleurs en Leonida , et on n’a trouvé aucun moyen de faire monter qui que ce soit dans notre voiture pour ce genre de service. Si ça se confirme, ce 6e opus serait donc le premier épisode en 3D à s’en passer.
Dans GTA 6, Rockstar n’a pas fermé tous les rideaux pour autant. On peut visiter plusieurs strip clubs à travers la carte, et il est toujours possible d’y payer un lap dance. Le jeu est même raccord avec son époque puisqu’on peut aussi se faire twerker dessus.
On reste prudent, puisque le jeu cache énormément de choses et qu’on n’exclut pas qu’un coin de la carte ou une quête annexe nous ait échappé. Mais après quelques tentatives habituelles de klaxonner à côté de PNJ féminin, ce qui est habituellement la démarche dans tous les GTA, celles-ci répondent « tu devrais avoir honte » , ce qui fait évidemment référence à notre sujet ici. La raison ici me semble plus qu’évidente, Rockstar ne voulait probablement pas ce genre d’histoire liée avec celle de Jason et Lucia . Ça évite aussi au studio de rejouer la même polémique qu’il y a douze ans.

x whatsapp-stroke copylink google Add Al Jazeera on Google info People pass giant billboards advertising the upcoming release of the video game Grand Theft Auto VI (GTA 6) in Melbourne, Australia, on November 18, 2026 [AFP] By Daniel Khalili-Tari Published On 18 Nov 2026 18 Nov 2026 It’s taken more than a decade and is estimated to have cost upwards of $1bn, but arguably the most anticipated release in gaming history is finally here.
Depending on where you live, Grand Theft Auto VI , better known as GTA 6, is now available to play. Digital intelligence company Sensor Tower estimates that Rockstar Games has already generated about $1.1bn in pre-order revenue, making it the largest pre-order launch in history.
So, what can gamers expect? And, more importantly, will it live up to the hype?
The latest instalment in the hugely popular franchise will be released across all regions at midnight local time tonight, Rockstar Games has confirmed. Those who have pre-ordered the game can already download it, allowing them to start playing GTA 6 as soon as the clock strikes 12am.
The action-adventure game will be available on PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X/S. Gamers will also be able to play it on Xbox One through Xbox Cloud Gaming.
Depending on the console you own, you’ll need up to 212GB of free storage space to download GTA 6. The process could take several hours, depending on your internet speed. Connecting your console directly to your router using an Ethernet cable could significantly reduce download times.
Video games have come a long way since the turn of the century, and so has GTA. The franchise has become the crown jewel of an industry that generated more than $201bn for the global economy in 2025, according to Newzoo.
In short, GTA is a cash cow, and its fans believe the profits are well-deserved. Reports suggest that GTA V Online, the previous instalment in the series, still generates an average of $1.3m a day for Rockstar Games.
GTA 6, like its predecessor, will feature more than one main protagonist. The game is set in the fictional Vice City, based on Miami, Florida.
The story centres on lovers and criminals Jason Duval and Lucia Caminos, whose lives resemble those of the notorious crime couple Bonnie and Clyde. The pair were gunned down by US law enforcement in 1934 during an ambush, after more than two years of robbing banks and killing police officers.
GTA 6 is set to feature even more crime and violence than previous editions, with the main story reportedly taking about 50 hours to complete. Meanwhile, achieving 100 percent completion could take as long as 200 hours.
The map is expected to be roughly twice the size of GTA V’s, with hundreds of enterable buildings, more than 170 animal species and enhanced artificial intelligence (AI), making it potentially the most realistic instalment in the franchise to date.
The wanted system, which is usually triggered when players commit crimes, has also been revamped. Players will be able to reach a wanted level of six stars for the most serious offences, while lesser crimes could attract as little as one star.
In a game where breaking the law is as normal as washing your face, Rockstar Games has focused on replicating the investigative processes used by real-life police. Computer-controlled characters, commonly known as non-playable characters (NPCs), will now be able to alert the police when they witness a crime.
Security cameras will also be able to capture Jason and Lucia, providing officers with additional intelligence. That means you’ll have to work harder to get the police off your tail. Officers will gather several clues about your misdeeds, forcing players to take multiple steps to avoid getting caught, including changing their appearance and switching vehicles.
Employers around the world could face staffing difficulties tomorrow. Opinium, a market research agency, estimates that 4.1 million working days in the United Kingdom alone could be lost due to employees calling in sick so they can spend the day playing GTA 6.
Those who are more organised have booked the big day off in advance, including Karl O’Connor, 34, who lives in Watford, a town just outside northwest London. O’Connor works full-time as a cinema manager and says that Grand Theft Auto: Vice City, released in 2002, is his favourite video game ever.

articles.t: GTA 6 struggles to hold 30 FPS on base PS5 'more often than expected'
articles.chapeau: GTA 6 holds a near flawless 30 FPS on PS5 Pro, while the base PS5 struggles more often than expected and drops during heavy action for a sustained period.
articles.txt:
Digital Foundry reports GTA 6 runs at 30 FPS on PS5 and PS5 Pro, but only the Pro reliably maintains that rate. The base console has minor dips and sustained sub-30 FPS performance during heavy action; Linneman described overall console performance as acceptable yet disappointing.

Grand Theft Auto 6 is a 30 FPS game on both PS5 and PS5 Pro, but according to Digital Foundry, only the PS5 Pro reliably holds that target, with the base PS5 struggling to maintain 30 FPS " more often than expected. "
The findings come from Digital Foundry's GTA 6 technical analysis, where John Linneman said he spent most of his time on the PS5 Pro, which he called " the best way to play this game by far. "
According to Linneman, the PS5 Pro delivers a " near flawless " 30 FPS with perfect frame pacing, and he played for more than 50 hours without seeing a single performance dip. Only by deliberately causing chaos with explosives could he push the PS5 Pro down to 24 FPS in what he described as the absolute worst case, an edge case that doesn't represent the game's average performance.
5 A GTA 6 driving scene shows a PS5 frame-rate reading of 26 FPS, below the game's 30 FPS target. VIEW GALLERY - 5 IMAGES The base PS5 is a different story. Linneman explained that the standard console gets " small dips throughout the experience, " which he described as " really very minor, " but added that he noticed them and that they slightly take you out of the experience. The bigger problem shows up in heavy action, as the same grenade launcher test that briefly tripped up the PS5 Pro caused sustained drops on the base PS5, with the whole sequence running below 30 FPS until the player leaves the area or is killed.
5 The same GTA 6 kitchen scene appears on PS5 and PS5 Pro; Digital Foundry says the Pro holds the game's 30 FPS target more reliably, while the base PS5 can dip during heavy action.
" If you're the type of GTA player that just wants to run around with a grenade launcher and blow stuff up, you might get performance like this ," Linneman said
5 The PS5 and PS5 Pro views show the same GTA 6 scene; Digital Foundry reports that the Pro holds its 30 FPS target more reliably than the base PS5. So, why is GTA 6 locked to 30 FPS at all? Linneman isn't convinced Rockstar could have hit 60 FPS " in a game of this scope on this class of hardware, " pointing to features like the physics-driven strand hair used on basically every NPC as one of many reasons.

articles.t: 'GTA 6' on Xbox Series S: How well it actually runs
articles.chapeau: Here's the verdict.
articles.txt:
Reading through Reddit, there is no shortage of concerns about how well Xbox Series S will or won’t run the game. As the release neared, fans seemed confident that Rockstar Games would ensure the game was playable, but opinions varied widely on what graphical sacrifices would be required for it to run, including reduced crowd density and scaled-back visuals.
How much time did I spend sweating the idea of crowd density? Too much. Did I ever think about it or care about it until Redditors said it’ll likely be less on the Series S? Not at all.
And yet, while it filled me with regret for not buying a PS5 last Black Friday before the price hikes arrived, it did not stop me from buying GTA 6 on Xbox Series S, debating whether or not to resist the pull off the New Zealand timezone trick to play it early, and preparing to explore Leonida.
And now, having played GTA 6 for a few hours, I can tell you everything you need to know about how it runs and how it feels.
I won’t keep you waiting: GTA 6 runs smooth as butter on Xbox Series S. There were no stutters, no lag or other slowdowns that pulled me out of the gameplay.
During a prologue that introduced me to protagonists Jason and Lucia, I quickly experienced a variety of locations in daytime and nighttime, as well as rainy weather. After that, I was able to play around Leonida and check out all the basic things that might catch your attention as you play: how the weather looks, flying down the road in a car through busy streets, random tasks around Jason's home.
In addition to moving quickly through various areas, I also took a moment to slow down. I watched a sunset by the water, went for a swim surrounded by fish, and observed how the environment affected Jason. Nothing slowed down, glitched out, or made me think anything other than I was playing a AAA game.
What I can’t tell you right now is how much better GTA 6 is or isn’t on PS5 or any of the higher-end consoles. We’re in the process of comparing the Xbox Series S version to the PS5 Pro version as we speak.
Rockstar has explicitly said the game will run best on PS5 consoles, with faster load times and technology that may improve resolution. The PS5 Pro version will also include ray tracing, making the lighting even more eye-catching. But both games will still be locked at 30 frames per second, according to Rockstar. The game developer did not say if any other sacrifices had to be made to get it to run on the Xbox Series S.
Regardless, what I can tell you is there is a good game waiting for you to play on Xbox Series S. If you don’t have the funds to upgrade your console, do not let comparison be the thief of joy.
GTA 6 is a generational moment in gaming and a cultural moment much larger than any game launch I’ve ever seen. The game is fun, the music is a vibe, and the world is immersive without feeling like a chore. I can't imagine waiting to play this if they have the means to do so right now.

GTA 6 arrive précédé d’une attente rare, au point d’avoir décroché huit nominations aux Game Awards 2026 avant même d’être testé , une omniprésence que nous relions à la crise de la presse jeu vidéo . Côté technique, une question revenait sans cesse depuis l’annonce de la PS5 Pro : le jeu tournerait-il à 60 images par seconde sur la console la plus puissante de Sony ? Rockstar a tranché dès le 10 novembre, à l’ouverture du préchargement, en annonçant 30 images par seconde sur toutes les consoles, PS5 Pro comprise.
Les premiers tests du jeu , publiés à la veille de sa sortie ce jeudi 19 novembre , permettent désormais de mesurer ce que la Pro apporte. Dans son analyse publiée ce mercredi 18 novembre, la chaîne britannique Digital Foundry , spécialisée dans la mesure des performances des jeux, confirme que GTA 6 reste bloqué à 30 images par seconde sur les deux consoles. L’écart entre PS5 et PS5 Pro se joue donc sur la netteté de l’image et la stabilité de l’animation.
Digital Foundry qualifie GTA 6 de « jeu le plus impressionnant visuellement de la génération ». Les deux consoles de Sony calculent pourtant l’image dans la même définition interne, du 1440p (2560 x 1440 pixels), à mi-chemin entre le Full HD et la 4K. Elles l’agrandissent ensuite pour remplir un téléviseur 4K, avec des méthodes différentes, que Rockstar a détaillées dans un entretien accordé au site spécialisé Wccftech ce mercredi. Sur PS5, le studio utilise sa propre technique basée sur le TAA, un anticrénelage temporel qui s’appuie sur les images précédentes pour lisser les contours, alors que la PS5 Pro passe par la deuxième version du PSSR , l’agrandissement par intelligence artificielle de Sony.

articles.t: GTA VI décroche 99/100 sur Metacritic et rejoint enfin le seul jeu qui régnait depuis 28 ans
articles.chapeau: Il aura fallu attendre vingt-huit ans pour voir un jeu se hisser aux côtés de Zelda: Ocarina of Time. À la veille de sa sortie, GTA VI compte déjà 145 critiques positives sur Metacritic. Qu’a donc trouvé la presse à Vice City pour lui faire un tel accueil ?
articles.txt:
Il aura fallu attendre vingt-huit ans pour voir un jeu se hisser aux côtés de Zelda: Ocarina of Time. À la veille de sa sortie, GTA VI compte déjà 145 critiques positives sur Metacritic. Qu’a donc trouvé la presse à Vice City pour lui faire un tel accueil ?
GTA VI et Ocarina of Time partagent la note de 99/100. © Clubic / Rockstar Games Treize ans qu’on attend de pouvoir écrire ces mots : demain, on retourne à Vice City. Ceux qui ont connu la ville sur PS2 y ont encore une station de radio préférée. D’autres ont grandi à Los Santos et s’apprêtent à la découvrir pour la première fois. On se demande tous un peu la même chose : une fois la manette en main, où est-ce qu’on file en premier ? Les journalistes qui ont déjà passé des dizaines d’heures sur GTA VI avaient un sacré avantage sur nous. À lire leurs tests, certains ont pourtant eu un mal fou à se décider à finir le jeu. Et les raisons qu’ils donnent sont encore plus réjouissantes que ce fameux 99/100.
BenQ BenQ iScreenBar : la barre lumineuse qui s’accorde avec l’iMac Des lignes en harmonie avec celles de l’ordinateur d’Apple, une conception rigoureuse, des matériaux sélectionnés, rien n’a été laissé au hasard, tout comme le service qu’elle rend une fois allumée !
Il faut remonter à 1998, à la Nintendo 64 et au jour où Link est sorti de la forêt pour découvrir la plaine d’Hyrule. Depuis, combien de jeux a-t-on vu passer sans que personne vienne déloger Ocarina of Time ? Ce 18 novembre, Metacritic attribue 99/100 à GTA VI sur PS5 . Le site le place en tête de son classement général, juste devant Zelda, qui affiche exactement la même note. Sur la fiche de GTA VI, les 145 critiques recensées à l’heure où nous écrivons sont toutes positives.
Lucia et Jason, main dans la main entre deux coups. © Rockstar Games Côté français, Gamekult , Gameblog et IGN France accordent tous trois à GTA VI la note maximale sur le barème de Metacritic. Mais ce qui retient Gamekult, c’est la patience nouvelle de Rockstar : à laisser souffler Jason et Lucia entre deux coups, le studio prend le risque de perdre les plus pressés et gagne le temps de nous attacher à eux. Gameblog en raconte l’autre bout, ce petit vide qui s’installe quand le générique défile et qu’on aimerait bien passer encore un moment avec le couple.
Trevor, Michael et Franklin avaient chacun leurs raisons de courir après l’argent. Jason et Lucia, eux, aimeraient en mettre assez de côté pour pouvoir un jour raccrocher ensemble. La nuance change jusqu’à la façon de jouer. The Verge raconte qu’entre deux grands braquages, on peut alimenter la cagnotte du couple en revendant une voiture volée ou en allant chercher un trésor au fond de la mer, le prochain gros coup peut attendre.
Pour renflouer la caisse du couple, on peut aussi aller voir ce qui se cache sous l’eau. © Rockstar Games Dans le Guardian , Keza MacDonald, qui a souvent levé les yeux au ciel devant la façon dont GTA traitait les femmes, raconte combien elle s’est attachée à Lucia et Jason. Le journaliste du Washington Post en donne peut-être la plus belle illustration : après 120 heures, il ne s’était toujours pas résolu à leur faire tuer des innocents, même par curiosité. Si vous avez déjà semé une pagaille monstre dans un GTA juste pour voir combien de temps vous tiendriez, vous mesurez le tour de force. Cette fois, on se soucie de ce qu’ils vont devenir.
The Verge raconte une anecdote qui va vous faire sourire : un SMS arrive alors qu’on conduit, on sort le portable pour le lire et, pendant ce temps, la voiture continue de rouler… On finit donc par faire dans GTA ce qu’on aurait dû faire depuis longtemps dans la vraie vie : se garer ! Ars Technica s’attarde de son côté sur les intérieurs et sur ces moments de calme que Rockstar glisse entre deux courses-poursuites. On peut aider un voisin à bricoler sa voiture ou faire griller des burgers au bord de l’eau…voilà qui explique peut-être pourquoi des journalistes pressés par une embargo, ont tout de même trouvé le temps de jouer au minigolf.
Vice City ne représente qu’une partie du terrain de jeu. Autour de la ville s’étend tout le Leonida. © Rockstar Games En France, Julien Chièze dit avoir bouclé l’histoire en une cinquantaine d’heures et passé près du double dans le Leonida. Il retient notamment le comportement des véhicules, assez différent d’un modèle à l’autre pour donner envie d’en essayer un de plus. Son enthousiasme a pourtant une limite : à force de soigner la mise en scène et de vouloir que tout s’enchaîne

L’attente touche au but pour les joueurs passionnés d’automobile, de belles mécaniques et de virées à haute vitesse en monde ouvert. Après avoir affiché complet durant plusieurs jours face à l’afflux massif de réservations, GTA 6 fait officiellement son retour en précommande sur Amazon France. L’enseigne vient en effet de réactiver la disponibilité de l’édition physique du jeu d’action-aventure de Rockstar Games, offrant une nouvelle occasion de sécuriser sa copie avant la sortie.

Si la saga Grand Theft Auto reste avant tout la référence du jeu d’action en monde ouvert, la conduite et la culture automobile constituent depuis toujours son ADN. Entre supercars inspirées des plus grands constructeurs européens, muscle cars américaines, préparation esthétique et poursuites musclées sur l’asphalte de Vice City et les longues lignes droites des Keys.

articles.t: GTA 6 reviews award 99 Metacritic score, topping GTA 4 to become Rockstar's top-rated
articles.chapeau: The GTA 6 Metacritic verdict is in, and reviews conclude it exceeds the loftiest expectations. On its release date, the title’s 99 Metascore beats Rockstar’s GTA 5, GTA 4, GTA 3, and Red Dead Redemption 2. It’s also tied with Zelda: Ocarina of Time for the aggregator’s top game of all time.
articles.txt:
As leaked, the GTA 6 review embargo expired when the title unlocked in New Zealand at midnight local time. Scores quickly populated Metacritic , averaging 99 and making it Rockstar ’s highest-rated game ever. Critics praise the massive Leonida map while dismissing concerns about a lackluster story .
Currently, the aggregator shows exclusively positive scores. Players who survived the long buildup to launch must wait 36 hours following the GTA 6 release date to submit user ratings. Even so, journalists are impressed and have awarded it Universal Acclaim status.
Despite fears that Rockstar would limit access to avoid leaks , Take-Two CEO Strauss Zelnick was anxious to read GTA 6 reviews. As it turns out, more than 140 outlets received Xbox or PS5 codes in recent weeks. After boasting about the studio’s past performance, Zelnick will welcome the latest Metacritic consensus.
ⓘ screenshot, Metacritic GTA 6 Metacritic score shown Jason and Lucia ’s crime epic edges out GTA 4 , which notched an average score of 98 in 1999. GTA 5 , GTA 3 , and Red Dead Redemption 2 are closely behind at 97. The game has also tied the 1998 N64 classic Zelda: Ocarina of Time for Metacritic’s highest-rated entry of all time .
Much larger than previous open-world maps , Leonida lives up to its promise, according to reviews. Each region has a unique feel, enhanced by an overhauled dynamic weather system . More buildings are explorable, addressing a popular fan request.
The fictional take on Florida can test the limits of Xbox and PS5 consoles. Although frame rates target 30 fps , release date performance impressions are reassuring. Digital Foundry measured sporadic dips below that mark, but the visuals generally remain smooth. Most importantly, controls are responsive even when rendering at below 60 fps.
When avoiding side activities, some GTA 6 reviews clock the time to complete Jason and Lucia’s story at around 60 hours. The overwhelming amount of content can stall the narrative’s pacing at times. Nevertheless, without revealing spoilers, the writing is compelling with unexpected twists.
Minor quibbles include a Vice City that's overly congested with cars and NPCs , which can slow missions. Regardless, Take-Two and Rockstar will be happy with the record-setting 99 GTA 6 Metacritic rating.

articles.t: Sortie de GTA 6 : démarrage en prison, braquage et fuite, musique dingue… On a vu les premières images du jeu de l’année
articles.chapeau: Grand Theft Auto 6, le jeu le plus attendu de l’année, voire de la décennie, est sorti à midi heure française en Nouvelle-Zélande. Donnant a
articles.txt:
Grand Theft Auto 6, le jeu le plus attendu de l’année, voire de la décennie, est sorti à midi heure française en Nouvelle-Zélande. Donnant aux joueurs les plus impatients les premières images.
Depuis des semaines, le monde du jeu vidéo n’attend que ça : ça y est, Grand Theft Auto (GTA) 6 est enfin disponible, treize ans après le cinquième volet . Et les premiers chanceux à pouvoir y jouer sont les Néo-Zélandais, grâce au décalage horaire. Rockstar Games, l’éditeur du jeu, a en effet choisi de sortir son produit phare le jeudi 19 novembre à minuit heure locale de chaque pays. En France donc, les premières images et diffusions en direct sont accessibles depuis ce mercredi midi.
Une attente interminable et enfin les premières images, y compris venant de streamers français étant parvenus à mettre leur console à l’heure néo-zélandaise . Un premier chargement long, très long, laissant craindre à un bug. Puis des paramètres à configurer, reculant encore l’arrivée à Vice City, lieu où se déroule le jeu.
🚨BREAKING: GTA 6 Game intro officially released pic.twitter.com/UsX6ndby4n
D’entrée, le ton est donné : une première cinématique. Une voiture en train d’être volée et les deux protagonistes : Lucia et Jason. La police qui intervient, un premier coup de poing et des forces de l’ordre tabassées. Le tout avec une musique immersive, mais bloquée chez certains streamers pour des raisons de droits d’auteur. Bienvenue dans GTA 6. La scène suivante montre les deux protagonistes chez eux… en pleine embrouille.
Après de nombreux crédits, une nouvelle cinématique transporte le joueur dans la vie de Lucia, neuf mois avant les premières scènes. Puis un nouveau flash-back. Lucia est cette fois en prison, tenue orange typique des détenus américains sur le dos.
Officially GTA 6 GAMEPLAY ( Intro Prison Scene #GTA6 ) pic.twitter.com/4R7FMkitnI
C’est là que le jeu commence vraiment. Lucia est contrôlable dans un monde ouvert, typique des GTA aux graphiques qui semblent soignés malgré les 30 images par seconde. Fidèle aux attentes sur ce point.
L’ellipse narrative prend fin, retour dans un bar avec Lucia. Quelques secondes après, on la retrouve pistolet à la main en plein braquage d’un point de retrait d’argent. Le joueur reprend la main en pleine fuite, coursée par la police. La première séquence avec Jason survient pour sa part sur un bateau, suivie d’une première mission où le joueur est amené (très) largement à utiliser son arme à feu et à esquiver les balles.
HAHAHA il a réussi à rater le tuto de GTA 6 😭 pic.twitter.com/RelSWLyi5z
Sans grande surprise, les premiers instants de ce nouvel opus transportent le joueur directement dans ce qu’il attendait : l’intrigue, le cadre, les armes… En moins d’une heure, il aura contrôlé deux personnages, une voiture, un bateau et… un hydravion avec lequel il est possible de s’amuser à faire des loopings ou de se crasher. Bref un monde où presque tout est permis dès les débuts.
Dès 11h45 heure française, mois d’une demi-heure donc avant le début des premières diffusions en direct, plus de 650 000 spectateurs de tous les pays attendaient déjà sur la plate-forme Twitch . Et le chiffre n’a cessé de monter pour dépasser le million à midi et les 2,5 millions à 12h40.
« Il y a de fortes chances que Twitch vive son plus grand record d’audience jamais enregistré », glissait au Parisien début novembre Dan Clancy, son PDG. D’après le cabinet spécialisé Sensor Tower, le jeu a été précommandé à plus de quinze millions d’exemplaires partout dans le monde.

articles.chapeau: From Justice's original score to radio stations hosted by Bad Bunny and Lana Del Rey, here's a guide to the music of "GTA 6."
articles.txt:
From the sun-soaked synth-pop of Vice City to surfing a sea of radio stations, music has always been an essential part of Rockstar Games' gritty, open-world franchise. And with Grand Theft Auto VI taking players back to Vice City, the sprawling soundtrack is shaping up to be just as ambitious as the game itself.
Rockstar has already revealed a 34-track album featuring artists like Travis Scott, Cardi B, and PinkPantheress, along with an original score composed by the French electronic duo Justice. Meanwhile, the game's fictional radio stations are bringing some familiar voices to the airwaves, including Robyn, Bad Bunny, and Lana Del Rey.
And that's just what we know so far. Ahead of GTA 6 's Nov. 19 release , we're keeping track of every confirmed song, artist, radio station, and celebrity DJ coming to Leonida. Consider this your unofficial guide to the sounds of Vice City.
Rockstar has announced Grand Theft Auto VI: The Album , a 34-track collection of original music arriving Nov. 19, the same day as the game.
The album features an eclectic mix of artists and genres , from hip-hop heavyweights Travis Scott and Cardi B to country star Morgan Wallen and Puerto Rican singer Rauw Alejandro. There's even a collaboration between CA7RIEL & Paco Amoroso, PinkPantheress, Fred again.., and French producer Etienne de Crécy. And somehow, someway, Morgan Wallen's single is the most-streamed track from the soundtrack on Spotify, with more than 25 million streams. Yung Lean, fight back!
"Sexy Magic" — CA7RIEL & Paco Amoroso, PinkPantheress, Fred again.. & Étienne de Crécy
"Flower in a Hurricane" — Justice feat. Tame Impala, SZA & King Gizzard & the Lizard Wizard
"Overtown Lights" — Stanley Clarke, Yussef Dayes & Robert Glasper
Fans can listen to the available singles on Rockstar's official GTA 6 music website , where the album is also available to pre-save or pre-order on vinyl and CD.
The French electronic duo Justice, consisting of Gaspard Augé and Xavier de Rosnay, is responsible for the original score of Grand Theft Auto VI .
Rockstar confirmed the news on Oct. 15 alongside the game's launch trailer , which features the debut of Justice's new single, "Flower in a Hurricane," featuring Tame Impala, SZA, and Australian psychedelic rock band King Gizzard & the Lizard Wizard.
It's a fitting collaboration for a game returning to Vice City, a fictional playground known for its vibrant nightlife and electronic music. Justice's signature blend of distorted synths, disco, and dance music feels particularly suited to Rockstar's radiant criminal underworld.
The duo previously collaborated with Tame Impala on "Neverender" from their 2024 album Hyperdrama . The song won Best Dance/Electronic Recording at the 2025 Grammys.
Rockstar has also confirmed that an official score album is on the way, although additional details, including its release date and tracklist, have yet to be announced.
The fictional radio stations are one of Grand Theft Auto 's most beloved features, and GTA 6 is bringing some major star power to the airwaves.
On Oct. 8, Rockstar unveiled six radio stations , each with its own musical identity and celebrity hosts. Among the biggest names are Bad Bunny, Robyn, Lana Del Rey, Burna Boy, and members of Slayer.
Here's a breakdown of the confirmed stations and their hosts :
Bad Bunny is bringing the sounds of Puerto Rico to Vice City. Alongside singer RaiNao, the superstar hosts Cocoteo FM, a station dedicated to modern Latin music, including reggaeton and other Caribbean sounds.
A familiar name for longtime Vice City fans, Flash FM returns with Swedish pop icon Robyn and model Alex Consani behind the microphone. The station promises a steady stream of pop music and dance-floor favorites.
Country music gets its own corner of Leonida with Back Country Radio, hosted by Morgan Wallen and Lana Del Rey. In perhaps the most unexpected casting choice, Del Rey's husband, Jeremy Dufrene, also makes an appearance as the station's " roving reporter, swamp meteorologist, and airboat captain ."
Afrobeats superstar Burna Boy teams up with DJ and producer Palms Trax for a station spotlighting amapiano, African classics, and other sounds from across the continent.
Metal fans aren't being left out. Slayer's Kerry King and Tom Araya host The Chamber , a station dedicated to heavy metal.

Deux cartes présentées comme des représentations de Leonida, l’État fictif dans lequel se déroule le jeu de Rockstar Games, circulent sur les réseaux sociaux. Elles montreraient un territoire particulièrement vaste, composé de cinq comtés, de grandes zones rurales, de marécages et de nombreuses routes. Leur origine exacte n’a cependant pas été authentifiée. Plusieurs éléments visuels semblent correspondre à des documents promotionnels officiels, mais cela ne suffit pas à confirmer l’ensemble des informations diffusées. Une chose est certaine : ces images relancent les discussions autour de l’un des jeux vidéo les plus attendus de ces dernières années.

Les documents sont au nombre de deux. Le premier présente Leonida sous la forme d’une carte géographique, avec ses routes, ses cours d’eau, ses îles et ses différentes zones naturelles.
Le second adopte une présentation plus illustrée et ferait apparaître cinq comtés. Cette organisation laisse entrevoir un territoire varié, au-delà de la seule ville de Vice City.
Les images ont notamment été relayées par un compte spécialisé dans l’actualité de Rockstar Games. Selon les informations qui les accompagnent, elles pourraient provenir de la « Vice City Collection », un ensemble de produits dérivés commercialisé autour du jeu.
Cette hypothèse explique pourquoi les joueurs leur accordent une certaine attention. La présence supposée de cartes dans un produit officiel renforcerait naturellement leur crédibilité.
Il reste toutefois nécessaire de rappeler que leur provenance exacte n’a pas été établie de manière indépendante. Il serait donc excessif de présenter ces documents comme une révélation officiellement confirmée par Rockstar Games.
Les cartes supposées mettent en évidence plusieurs caractéristiques géographiques qui correspondent à l’univers déjà présenté pour « GTA VI ».
Leonida s’inspire de la Floride, et Vice City constitue l’une de ses principales destinations. Les nouvelles images suggèrent que l’exploration pourrait s’étendre bien au-delà de cet environnement urbain.
De vastes zones rurales apparaissent au nord et à l’ouest. Des marécages seraient également présents dans le sud, tandis que plusieurs réseaux routiers relieraient les différents secteurs.
Les cartes montrent aussi des îles, des voies d’eau et des infrastructures de transport. Un grand aéroport serait notamment situé au sud-ouest de Vice City.
Ces éléments donnent l’impression d’un territoire conçu pour proposer des environnements très différents, entre ville, campagne, zones humides et littoral.
La variété géographique pourrait avoir une influence importante sur l’expérience de jeu. Dans la série Grand Theft Auto, les déplacements et la découverte du monde ouvert occupent une place centrale.
